A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SaMyNa, with matching core methods and benchmarks. Their main text and appendices support reliable comparison, including the rotated tables. Clipped BAR scores in v2 Table 5 are available fully in Table 25.

before.justification: v1 reports original keyword-discovery experiments, subgroup accuracies, visualizations, and appendix ablations on Waterbirds, CelebA, BAR and ImageNet-A.

after.justification: v2 retains original bias-discovery experiments and adds debiasing results, direct B2T comparisons, a human annotation study, captioner comparisons and additional ablations.

M1.justification: The core discovery pipeline remains, but v2 adds CLIP-based subgroup pseudo-labeling followed by GroupDRO training (Sec. 4.3), substantially extending the procedure to mitigation. Appendix F introduces an optional randomized-label threshold-selection procedure. Section 3.2.5 also replaces explicit target-class keyword filtering with allowing users to disregard such keywords.

E1.justification: The four image benchmarks and their classification tasks remain, including balanced Waterbirds and the existing ImageNet-A cases. The new 20-participant keyword-annotation study on three retained datasets adds a limited human-task and population extension (Sec. 5.4).

E2.justification: v2 adds a debiasing comparison against ERM, LISA, GroupDRO, George, JTT, CNC, LfF, DebiAN and B2T+GDRO (Table 1), largely using cited baseline results. It also directly evaluates B2T on BAR and matched CelebA samples (Appendix D), and compares ClipCap with LLaVA (Appendix B). These comparisons were absent from v1.

E3.justification: v2 introduces GroupDRO evaluation using unbalanced average and worst-group accuracy, matched-sample B2T comparisons, a stratified 195-image BAR validation split, and a 20-participant survey protocol. Appendix F adds a randomized-label control. Captioning is reported as using one generic prompt instead of v1's dataset-specific prompts; this establishes a reported setting revision, without proving which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test removal of shared-feature subtraction, joint hyperparameter effects, captioner adequacy, B2T sample efficiency and failure cases, and randomized-label threshold calibration. The original aligned/conflicting accuracy diagnostic is removed. ViT, balanced-Waterbirds, nails-versus-mushrooms and k analyses already existed in v1; their relocation is not an addition.

E5.justification: Appendix F newly estimates a randomized-label null distribution and uses its maximum for class-specific thresholds, with distribution standard deviations reported. This adds statistical calibration. Plus/minus reporting already existed in v1 Table 12; v2's additional error-bearing rows do not establish a new uncertainty practice or increased runs. Neither version specifies run or seed counts.

E6.justification: v1 Table 1's vanilla subgroup accuracies disappear; v2 Table 1 adds GroupDRO results, including 90.60 and 90.62 worst-group accuracy on CelebA and Waterbirds, and 71.26 average accuracy on BAR. Human, captioner and B2T results are added. Existing keyword outputs also change, such as CelebA's woman score from 0.48667 to 0.39947. These are revised outputs under changed reported settings, not established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly adds the binary-class symmetry argument: centered class embeddings point in opposite directions, producing opposite cosine scores and reversed keyword rankings (Appendices C.2.4 and D). The principal equations otherwise retain their mathematical substance; expanded averaging explanations and notation changes do not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: v1 chiefly claims interpretable bias discovery and model diagnosis. v2 adds competitive or state-of-the-art debiasing performance as an explicit abstract and introduction contribution when SaMyNa is coupled with GroupDRO. The abstract also drops v1's 'first tool' novelty assertion. Training-time and inference-time diagnosis remain core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning inherited captioner biases and human interpretation (Sec. 5.6), plus retraining and computational restrictions on automatic thresholds (Appendix F). It expands explanations of imbalanced embedding aggregation and B2T's filtering and sampling failures. The earlier explanation attributing stronger similarity scores to larger text encoders is dropped.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the exact captioning prompt, confidence-based selection of misclassified examples, preprocessing source, BAR GroupDRO hyperparameters, timing hardware and batch size, and human-survey instructions. These substantially expand reproducibility information. v1's 300-token limit is no longer stated. The default embedding-model link and promise of code release upon acceptance remain unchanged.

R1.justification: B2T was already cited in v1, but v2 substantially expands positioning against it around validation requirements, captioning cost, keyword filtering and modality flexibility (Introduction and Appendix D). It revises the description from captioning the training set to the validation set. New references include Guimard et al.'s classifier-to-bias framework, margin-based noisy-label work, ClipCap and additional debiasing comparators.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: existing ViT, balanced-Waterbirds, nails-versus-mushrooms and k analyses move into a new main-text analysis section, while visual feedback moves to Appendix A. Contributions and method explanations are rewritten and expanded, and the appendices are reorganized around comparisons, ablations, survey details and calibration.

P2.justification: v2 adds extensive comparison and human-study tables, caption examples, ablation plots and calibration histograms. It combines the Waterbirds and CelebA plots, redraws the pipeline diagram, incorporates existing heatmaps into Figure 1, expands the appendix heatmap examples, and introduces landscape result tables. Table 5 has a localized clipping problem.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's lack of direct comparative validation through B2T comparisons and downstream GroupDRO tests, supplemented by human judgments, targeted ablations and explicit captioner limitations. These strengthen evidence for usefulness and interpretability despite removal of the original subgroup-accuracy diagnostic. Remaining weaknesses include unspecified run counts and overbroad superiority wording: Table 1 gives Waterbirds worst-group accuracy of 90.62 for SaMyNa versus 90.70 for B2T+GDRO.
